title: AURA Composer command payloads (Plan H1)
description: Request/reply shapes for the five additive composer commands — `harmony_get`, `harmony_set`, `composer_palette`, `composer_suggest`, `composer_generate`. Source of truth: `src-tauri/src/control/composer.rs` (the wire types) over `src-tauri/src/theory/` (the meanings). An emitter contract: `additionalProperties` is not closed (debt D-06). The document itself lives in harmony.schema.json. NOTE what is NOT here: annotations are returned WITH a reply for display and are never document state (ruling H-6), and generated notes are ordinary MIDI clips described by midi-clip.schema.json — there is no generated-clip type.

harmonyView.title: harmony_get / harmony_set reply
harmonyView.description: Everything the COMPOSER panel draws. All of it is backend-derived: the widget contains no theory (ADR 0006).

key.description: Canonical key in force at the request's `atTicks`.

keySignature.description: Sharps (positive) or flats (negative): the fifths index of the relative major tonic.

wedges.description: The twelve circle-of-fifths slots, clockwise, SPELLED FOR THIS KEY (E major gets D#, Bb major gets Eb).

neighbours.description: Keys one easy move away, each with why and its pivot chords.

schemas.description: The named progressions, as Roman numerals that transpose into any key.

inKey.description: Inside the key's diatonic arc. Exactly seven of the twelve are, which is the fact the widget draws.

chord.description: The key's own chord here, when in the arc.

borrowedChord.description: What this slot offers as a borrowed chord when it is outside the arc.

isTonic.description: The widget rotates THIS slot to the top rather than hard-coding C.

spanView.description: One chord region, analysed in the key in force at its own tick.

roman.description: Roman numeral, with figured bass for an inversion (`V65`).

why.description: One concrete sentence — the teaching payload.

numerals.description: Space-separated numerals, each optionally `*bars`: `"I7*4 IV7*2 I7*2 V7 IV7 I7 V7"`.

minor.description: Written for a minor tonic. Asked for against the other mode, the schema resolves in the RELATIVE key and the reply says so.

paletteView.title: composer_palette reply
paletteView.description: Which notes may be played at a tick, and why (ruling H-9). Twelve entries, pitch-class order.

tpc.description: Best spelling in context (`Bb`, not `A#`, in a flat key).

role.description: `avoid` is a key tone a SEMITONE ABOVE a chord tone — Berklee's avoid note, and the rule the whole feature's credibility rests on.

degree.description: Degree label relative to the chord: `1`, `b7`, `#11`.

score.description: 0..1. Composed of the grammar's transition weight, how canonical the degree is, common tones and novelty — and `why` states the breakdown, because a ranking a user cannot interrogate is a black box.

parts.description: Empty = all four. Every part lands in ONE transaction (ruling H-7).

plan.description: A schema id, `"circle"` / `"circle:cw"`, or `"functional:<0-100>"`. None = keep the harmony document and write parts against it.

seed.description: None = derived from the request, so the same request stays reproducible (ruling H-4).

trackIds.description: Reuse a track per part instead of creating one: `{"melody": "<trackId>"}`. A non-midi or unknown track is rejected and NOTHING is written.

writeHarmony.description: Defaults to true when `plan` is given (the progression is the point), false otherwise.

seed.description: What produced this — store it and the take is recoverable.

bars.description: What was actually written: the HARMONY decides the length, not the request.

annotation.description: Why a generator did what it did. Display only — never persisted, never a field on a clip (ruling H-6).

key.description: The key the progression is actually IN — a minor-mode schema asked for in a major key resolves in the relative minor.
